transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just can't keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like, I'll try to tell someone about my overnight shift—I'm an orderly, so I work these really long hours on the ward. The lights there at 3 AM are this harsh fluorescent, and it makes the paint colors on the walls look totally different, kind of this sickly green. Which actually reminds me of the turf we used to play soccer on back in high school. Man, I miss playing soccer. We had this one game where it rained so hard the ball wouldn't even roll... but anyway, yeah, I'll start talking about my shift, and then suddenly I'm jumping to soccer, or paint colors, or the patient charts I was supposed to be organizing, and... I just look up and I can see everyone getting lost. They just stare at me. I just can't keep it straight.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being put into your head by someone else, or like someone can hear your thoughts, or even that thoughts are being taken out of your mind?

No, I don't... I don't think anyone is putting thoughts in there, or taking them out. If they could hear my thoughts, that would be like one of those old sci-fi movies, you know? My older brother used to collect all those DVDs. He had shelves and shelves of them in our shared bedroom growing up. Actually, DVDs are pretty much completely useless now, right? Everything is just streaming. We actually tried to get a streaming stick working on the TV in the day room for the patients on my unit, but the Wi-Fi on the fourth floor is just a total dead zone. The maintenance guy, Carl, he said it's because of the reinforced concrete walls they poured back in the seventies. Carl knows literally every inch of that building, he even showed me where the old laundry chutes used to be before they sealed them up... but, uh, wait. What were you asking me? Oh, right, my thoughts. No, nobody is taking them. They're just my own thoughts. Just... really messy ones.
Have you ever experienced things that others around you don’t seem to experience—like hearing voices when no one is speaking, or seeing things that others don’t see?

Voices? No, I don't hear anything like that. Just regular people talking. I mean, sometimes at work, the intercom system on the ward gets this weird static, and it almost sounds like someone is whispering. But it's just the old wiring. The hospital is so old, man. They brought this electrician in a couple weeks ago to look at it, and he had this massive leather toolbelt. It looked exactly like the one my dad used to wear when we’d work on his truck. 

It was a '98 Chevy Silverado, cherry red. We spent a whole summer trying to rebuild the transmission in the driveway, and it was so hot out the asphalt actually melted a little bit under the jack stands. My mom was so mad about those dents in the driveway... she tried to fill them with some cheap tar patch she bought at Home Depot, but it never really matched the color, you know? It just looked like these big black puddles right where we used to play basketball. I used to have a pretty decent jump shot before I messed up my ankle... but, uh... what were we talking about? Seeing things? No, I don't see anything that isn't there either. Just normal stuff.
Have you ever found yourself acting in a way that others might describe as strange, or had periods where you felt slowed down, unresponsive, or like you weren't moving normally?

Strange? I mean, I guess so, yeah. At work, I've caught myself just... rocking back and forth in the hallway. Or there's this one patient who taps his fingers on the table all the time, and I'll realize I'm standing right next to him, copying the exact same tapping rhythm. He always taps with his index and middle finger, like he's playing a tiny piano. I tried to learn piano when I was a kid, actually. My grandma had this huge upright Yamaha in her living room, right next to this massive fern she kept alive for like, twenty years. The leaves on that thing were huge, almost looked prehistoric, you know? Like a dinosaur could just pop out from behind it. I used to watch Jurassic Park all the time on VHS. The tracking was always messed up on the T-Rex scene, so the screen would get all fuzzy and jumpy right when it roared. It's funny how VHS tapes used to do that, you'd have to physically adjust the little dial on the VCR to fix it. Kids today don't even know what a VCR is... 

But anyway, yeah, I'll be doing that tapping thing, or sometimes I'll just be standing there with my latex gloves only half on, like my hands are just stuck. And I know I'm supposed to be doing my rounds, checking the rooms, but I just... freeze up. Like I'm not moving right.
Have you ever felt down, depressed, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?

Yeah... yeah, I have. It's like this heavy, empty feeling, you know? Most days it's just there from the second I wake up. I drag myself to work, but after my shift... I'll just sit in my car in the parking lot and cry. I can't even put the key in the ignition to drive home. My car is this old Honda Civic, it's got that weird smell in the upholstery, kind of like stale coffee and old textbooks. I bought it off this guy on Craigslist who said he used it to deliver pizzas in college. You can still see a little grease stain on the passenger seat where I guess a box leaked once. I tried scrubbing it out with this heavy-duty carpet cleaner, the kind that foams up real big? But it just made the stain spread out and look like a weird map of Australia. I always wanted to go to Australia, actually. See the Great Barrier Reef before it all dies off. I watched this documentary about coral bleaching, and it's crazy how they just turn stark white when the water gets too warm. It’s like all the life just drains right out of them... kind of like... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right. Yeah, the heavy feeling. It's been going on for a long time. Months, really. Just... empty.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things that used to make you happy, like playing soccer or watching movies, for example?

Yeah... I don't really do much of anything anymore. I used to sketch a lot, like these big murals, and I'd cook dinner for my friends... play soccer on the weekends. But now, it all just feels completely pointless. I don't even reply to my friends' texts. I just sit in my apartment and ignore my phone. My phone screen is actually shattered right now, right across the front camera. I dropped it when I was trying to carry a bunch of groceries up the stairs. I had this huge bag of oranges, and the bottom of the paper bag just gave out. Oranges were rolling everywhere, down the steps, into the hallway... my neighbor's cat actually came out and started batting one around. It was this fluffy orange tabby, kind of looked like Garfield. I loved reading Garfield comics when I was a kid. The Sunday papers always had them in full color, and my dad would let me pull that section out before he read the news. He always read the sports section first, though. He was obsessed with the Chicago Bears. Had this giant foam bear claw he’d wear during games... but, yeah. I just don't care about sketching or soccer or any of it anymore. Just stay inside.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like sketching or playing soccer?

I think I just said that, didn't I? Yeah... I used to do all those things. Sketching those big murals, having people over for dinner, the weekend soccer games... but it's all just pointless now. I don't even look at my phone when people text me. I just leave it on the coffee table. The coffee table I have is this heavy oak thing I found at a thrift store. It has these clawed feet, like an eagle or a dragon or something, gripping little glass balls. It's really heavy, took three of us to carry it up to my apartment when I first moved in. That was back when I actually had the energy to move furniture around. We ordered pizza after, from this place down the street that does this amazing deep dish. They put the sauce on top of the cheese, which sounds weird, but it actually keeps the crust from getting soggy. The crust is the best part, honestly. If the crust is bad, the whole pizza is ruined. I tried making pizza dough from scratch once, but it didn't rise right. It ended up looking like a giant, flat cracker. I think I killed the yeast because the water was too hot. You have to use lukewarm water, like, barely warm to the touch... 

But yeah, I don't do any of that anymore. No cooking, no soccer, no sketching. I just stay in my apartment and ignore everything. It's just... I don't see the point.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energetic, like you didn’t need much sleep, or your mood was extremely up and down—like a high that felt out of control?

No... no, I don't think so. I'm just always tired. I never get that energetic feeling. Actually, the orderly I work with at the hospital—he's always bouncing off the walls. He drinks those huge energy drinks, the ones in the neon cans that look like battery acid. I tried one once before a shift, but it just made my heart beat really fast and my hands shake. I couldn't even hold the food trays steady when I was delivering them to the patients. One of the trays almost slipped, and this little cup of green Jell-O slid right off and bounced on the floor. It didn't even break apart, just jiggled there like a little alien blob. I used to love Jell-O when I was a kid, especially the red kind. We'd have it at every family barbecue. My uncle used to make this weird Jell-O salad with shredded carrots and marshmallows in it. Who puts carrots in Jell-O? It's just wrong. It completely ruins the texture. Texture is so important with food, you know? Like, if a grape is squishy, I can't eat it. It has to be firm and snap when you bite into it... 

But, uh, no. I never feel high or out of control like that. Just... heavy. All the time.
Have you noticed that you’re doing much less than usual, or that even small tasks feel overwhelmingly difficult?

Yeah... yeah, everything is just... too hard. Even just getting up to get a glass of water feels like I have to climb a mountain. I haven't done laundry in... I don't even know how long. The pile in my closet is just growing. It's mostly my scrubs from work, those light blue ones. They're so uncomfortable, the fabric is really stiff and scratchy, especially around the collar. I tried washing them with extra fabric softener once, this lavender-scented kind that my mom always used. She loved lavender. She grew it in the backyard, right next to the tomatoes. The tomatoes always got eaten by these big, ugly green caterpillars with little horns on them. Tomato hornworms, I think they're called. They blend in perfectly with the leaves, so you don't even see them until half the plant is gone. I used to pick them off with a stick and throw them over the fence into the empty lot next door. That lot was always full of weeds and old tires... people just dumped their junk there. Someone even left a whole rusted-out washing machine once. 

But yeah... I'm just not doing much of anything. Small tasks, big tasks... it doesn't matter. It's all just too much.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating much less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Yeah... I guess so. I barely get hungry anymore. Most days I just drink coffee at work, maybe grab some of those peanut butter crackers from the vending machine if I remember. My clothes have gotten really loose. My belt is on the last hole and my pants still slide down. It's one of those cheap leather belts that starts peeling after a few months, you know? The brown kind of flakes off and leaves this weird gray material underneath. I bought it at this discount store near the bus stop. That bus stop is always freezing in the winter because the glass on one side of the shelter is shattered. Someone threw a rock through it a long time ago and the city never fixed it. There's always this old guy waiting there, feeding the pigeons. He brings whole bags of bread crusts. Pigeons are kind of gross when you really look at them, they have those weird iridescent feathers on their necks but their feet look like scaly little dinosaur claws. I read somewhere that birds actually evolved from dinosaurs, which makes sense if you look at a chicken running... 

But yeah, I'm just not eating much. I just don't have an appetite.

But yeah, I'm just not eating much. I just don't have an appetite.
